claims.text: Friction Stir Processing can repair a damaged CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy-alloy component.
FSP will refine the microstructure of the CoCrFeMnNi repair zone.
FSP will eliminate hot cracking in the repaired component.
FSP will restore mechanical properties superior to those of traditional fusion-weld repairs.
The as-cast damaged CoCrFeMnNi component has a fine dendritic microstructure.
The CoCrFeMnNi component is prone to hot cracking when fusion welded.
Tool rotational speeds of 600–900 rpm, with adjusted traverse speed, can maintain local processing temperature at approximately 0.6–0.7 Tm.
An inert processing atmosphere mitigates oxidation during FSP.
FSP will produce a dynamically recrystallized, fine-grained stir-zone microstructure.
The FSP stir zone will be free of segregation and vulnerable melting zones.
FSP imparts severe localized plastic deformation and frictional heating.
Localized plastic deformation and frictional heating induce dynamic recrystallization in the repair zone.
Because FSP is a solid-state intervention, it bypasses the melt–solidification cycle associated with conventional fusion welding.
The melt–solidification cycle in conventional fusion welding is responsible for hot cracking.
Relative to fusion-weld repair, the FSP-repaired zone will have enhanced toughness, improved fatigue resistance, and a more homogeneous microstructure.
The FSP-repaired component will sustain performance under aggressive operating conditions.
Traditional fusion-welding repair causes prolonged high-temperature exposure, compositional inhomogeneity, coarse dendritic structures, and a critical risk of hot cracking.
FSP is well established for alloys similar to CoCrFeMnNi.
Complex or non-planar component geometries may require special tooling, process modification, and calibration.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that success will be ensured in high-temperature and high-stress environments, whereas the uncertainty field says additional calibration and validation are still required under service conditions and for complex geometries.
